channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: US Stands by Oil Deal With Venezuelan Energy Mogul Betancourt
item.description: The Trump administration defended its decision to partner with a controversial investor on 17 oil fields in Venezuela, saying he is uniquely positioned to help revitalize the nation’s aging wells and restore the flow of crude.
item.dc:creator: Skylar Woodhouse and Peter Millard

item.title: Massachusetts Senate Race Tests Two Big Trends of the 2026 Midterms
item.description: If the polls are correct, an 80-year-old incumbent will move ahead to November’s general election.
item.dc:creator: Nancy Cook

item.title: Hollywood Studios Eye Federal Incentives as Jon Voight Group Pushes Legislation
item.description: A group led by actor Jon Voight is hoping to get legislation introduced this month in Congress that would create new federal tax incentives for film and TV production in the US, after receiving an endorsement from President Donald Trump this week.
item.dc:creator: Christopher Palmeri

item.title: US, Iran Re-Escalate Conflict | Bloomberg Businessweek Daily 9/1/2026
item.description: US-Iran tensions over the Strait of Hormuz heightened after a flurry of military strikes at the start of the week. Bloomberg News Senior Editor Wendy Benjaminson explains what led to the new uptick in fighting following weeks of relative calm. Then, Bloomberg TV & Radio Economics & Policy Correspondent Mike McKee and Bloomberg Rates Reporter Michael MacKenzie react to the bond market's spike and what it sets up for September as investors brace for another Fed meeting. Plus, Voya Financial CEO Heather Lavallee explains the trends she is seeing in Gen Z saving for retirement more than any other generation. Finally, Amazon Web Services General Manager of Media, Entertainment, Games and Sports Samira Bakhtiar discusses how the company is pioneering AI in entertainment production and content creation. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Zelenskyy Threatens to Shut Air Traffic Over Russia With Drones
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned airlines to avoid Russian airspace as he threatened to respond to Moscow’s escalating missile attacks by crowding its skies with drones.
item.dc:creator: Aliaksandr Kudrytski

item.title: House Republicans 'Very Optimistic' That Party Will Hold Control of Congress
item.description: Indiana Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman said that his party is feeling 'very optimistic' that they can retain control of both the House and the Senate in the midterms, but acknowledged that candidates have work to do on the campaign trail to make it happen. The congressman also discussed US strikes in Iran, saying that the Iranian regime is trying to drag the conflict out as long as possible. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Launches New Iran Strikes | Radio Balance of Power: Early Edition 9/1/2026
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu and Kailey Leinz discuss the latest from Iran. On today's show, Republican Congressman Marlin Stutzman of Indiana, Democratic Congresswoman Madeleine Dean of Pennsylvania, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Beacon Global Strategies Energy Practice Lead Clayton Seigle. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California Lawmakers Adjourn Without Voting on Wildfire Bill
item.description: The California Assembly adjourned without passing a revamp of the state’s wildfire response, sending up shares in two key power utilities, PG&E Corp. and Edison International.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Oxford and Michelle Ma

item.title: House GOP Majority Shrinks as Georgia Democrat Is Sworn In
item.description: Everton Blair joined the House Tuesday, narrowing Speaker Mike Johnson’s majority for the final legislative stretch before the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Rachel Schilke

item.title: Congress Sends Funding Bill to Avert US Shutdown to Trump
item.description: Congress cleared funding legislation to avert an Oct. 1 government shutdown, sidestepping, at least temporarily, the partisan warfare that led to repeated disruptions over the last year.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: Kuwait Decree Allows Government to Borrow From Wealth Fund
item.description: Kuwait’s government has issued a decree allowing it to borrow from its $1 trillion-plus sovereign wealth fund in order to support state finances, as Gulf economies deal with the impact of the US-Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Fiona MacDonald

item.title: Putin, Xi Discussed Possible APEC Talks With Trump, Russia Says
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed the possibility of holding a trilateral meeting with their US counterpart Donald Trump when China hosts the APEC summit later this year, according to Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov.
item.dc:creator: Ilya Arkhipov

item.title: Trump Steps Up New York Immigration Fight With 2,100 Arrests
item.description: The Trump administration said it arrested more than 2,100 immigrants across New York in a monthlong operation, intensifying a fight with state and city leaders over their refusal to more closely assist with the federal immigration crackdown.
item.dc:creator: Myles Miller

item.title: Iran Nuclear Status Unknown With US War Unresolved, IAEA Says
item.description: Iran is continuing to deny international inspectors access to its nuclear facilities, the United Nations atomic watchdog reported, amid little sign that Tehran and Washington are close to finding a way to end their six-month war.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Tirone

item.title: US, Iran Escalate Attacks as Fighting Around Strait Heats Up
item.description: The US launched a fresh wave of strikes against targets in Iran and the Islamic Republic said it retaliated, as the back-and-forth of fighting between the two escalated sharply.
item.dc:creator: Kate Sullivan, Grant Smith and Eltaf Najafizada

item.title: Surge in UK Borrowing Costs Halves Government’s Fiscal Headroom
item.description: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham was confronted by the harsh reality of Britain’s weak public finances on his return to parliament on Tuesday as the global selloff in government bonds left him facing a £12 billion problem.
item.dc:creator: Philip Aldrick, Georgia Hall and George Nixon

item.title: Burnham Says Water Central to UK Plan for Public Control
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the water industry “stands as a leaking monument” to what he sees as the failure of decades of privatization in Britain, signaling he’s open to nationalizing the industry.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham, Jessica Shankleman and Joe Mayes

item.title: Bessent Says Hormuz Will Be ‘Worthless’ as Oil Bypasses It
item.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent dismissed the importance of the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, saying the crucial waterway for Persian Gulf energy that’s been controlled by Iran during the recent conflict will be bypassed by oil pipelines.
item.dc:creator: Yash Roy

item.title: Germany Blames Russia for Attempted Drone Attack, Expects More
item.description: Germany’s government said an investigation found that Russia is behind a failed drone attack at an airport in Leipzig last month and that the Kremlin is likely to step up hybrid aggression.
item.dc:creator: Michael Nienaber and Arne Delfs

item.title: Military Expects UK to Spend 3% of GDP on Defense By 2030
item.description: The British military still expects Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey to commit to spending 3% of domestic output on defense by 2030, despite accusations that he was backsliding on his ambition to hit that target.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham
